correctness.rationale: The proof classifies all inside and outside Lie subalgebras via two eigenspaces of the adjoint action; counts mixed closure through invariant superspaces and quotient graph maps; counts outside pair closure using the eigenspace union in the difference quotient and exact Gaussian intersection multiplicities. In the large-field limit only the (2,2) and (2,3)/(3,2) boundary values tie the inside/outside degree exponents. Their leading favorable/total coefficients are respectively 10/25 and 7/16, while strict inside dominance yields limit one. The independent RREF bracket checker agrees in five small configurations, including q=2, (a,b)=(2,2), and q=3, (a,b)=(2,2). Exhaustive finite checks support, not replace, the all-field symbolic argument.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The November 8 full text treats aff_1 plus r central generators: its noncentral eigenspace has dimension one, and its parity limit therefore covers the min(a,b)=1 boundary after scalar shift. The October Jordan-chain full text covers a single Jordan block and general scalar shifts, not two nontrivial eigenspace multiplicities. Neither offers a theorem implying the present Gaussian intersection sums and phase limits for a,b>=2.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The source paper establishes the definition and some distinct families, and the 3D and rank-one central stabilization statements are strict lower-dimensional/one-eigenspace-multiplicity boundary cases. A result for a=1 does not imply a,b>=2: for example its 0 or 1/4 field-limit spectrum cannot yield 2/5 or 7/16. The Jordan-chain lattice has only a chain of invariant ideals and different combinatorics. Hence the new surviving claim is not a simple already-covered specialization of these results.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A diagonal action with distinct eigenvalues has the same subalgebra and permutability relation as the action after adding a scalar multiple of the identity. Thus two nonzero eigenvalues can be reduced to the central-plus-scalar case; this equivalence is explicitly credited. A single Jordan block, even up to scalar shifts, cannot become a split two-eigenspace action of multiplicities a,b>=2: their invariant-subspace lattices differ.

originality.rationale: The first public September 2026 primary article defines the quantity and handles other selected Lie algebras. Complete full-text comparisons with the published 2026 three-dimensional record, 2026 Jordan-block record, and 2026 rank-one central-stabilization record show that all cases with one eigenspace dimension one and the universal scalar-shift identity are covered and explicitly excluded from this theorem. The surviving a,b>=2 two-parameter census and phase limits (2/5, 7/16, 1) were not implied by these verified prior results. Indexed-search noncoverage is not proof of absolute priority; inaccessible or unindexed further sources remain risk.
residual_risks: An earlier 4D diagonal-action calculation mentioned within the November 8 record was not independently located; our theorem excludes all 4D cases and lower-dimensional consequences.
Older unindexed subalgebra-lattice enumerations might imply a broader higher-rank formula; targeted search and primary comparisons did not locate such coverage.
No independent specialist priority assessment has been made.

value.rationale: This is a natural two-parameter extension of the current rank-one central-stabilization subalgebra-permutability problem, not a singled-out arbitrary example. The all-prime-power closed finite-sum census is accompanied by a sharp structural phase diagram: the rational limits 2/5 and 7/16 arise from distinct collisions of Gaussian dimension strata, while every other a,b>=2 family tends to one. These values distinguish higher noncentral rank from the known one-direction parity law and provide a reusable count for arbitrary field order and dimensions.
